stages.purpose: Collect the nearest checked report example, sanitized output summary, and redacted diagnostics.
Classify the report as expected behavior that can be clarified in docs or report examples.
Reply with public-safe wording and ask for redacted diagnostics only if local output differs.
Record whether the docs clarification shipped or is queued, then link the public-safe follow-up.
Confirm the follow-up is low-priority docs clarification before opening a backlog record.
Record the public-safe docs backlog artifact and the checks needed after copy changes.
Revisit whether the docs backlog item remains active or should close with no action.

title: Plausible false-positive boundary needs fixture evidence

stages.purpose: Collect the smallest sanitized reproduction, redacted doctor output, and tune evidence.
Classify the report as a safe boundary candidate before changing rule behavior.
Tell the reporter that a pass or quiet-pass fixture should prove the boundary first.
Record that a redacted fixture backlog item exists and the rule remains unchanged.
Confirm the follow-up is medium-priority fixture backlog before changing any matcher.
Record the public-safe fixture backlog artifact and the expected pass or quiet-pass boundary.
Revisit whether the fixture backlog item remains active or is already covered elsewhere.

title: Repeated sanitized surprises need rule review

stages.purpose: Collect repeated sanitized examples, redacted doctor output, and tune fixture evidence.
Classify repeated reports as a candidate for guidance or matching review.
Explain that maintainers need multiple sanitized examples before changing guidance or matching.
Record that a rule-review candidate was opened and fixture evidence will be compared.
Confirm the follow-up is high-priority rule review backed by repeated sanitized reports.
Record the public-safe rule-review backlog artifact and the fixture evidence to compare.
Revisit whether repeated evidence still warrants rule review before any behavior change.
